findings.title: get_monitor_environment_context discards the humanized config copy it just built
findings.body: In `get_monitor_environment_context` the code copies `monitor.config` into a local `config` variable and replaces `schedule_type` with its human-readable display value, but the returned context dict uses `monitor_environment.monitor.config` (the raw, unmodified config) instead of the local `config`. As a result the `schedule_type` humanization never takes effect in the monitor context attached to occurrence events — consumers see the raw integer schedule type. The return should use the local `config` variable. This bug was carried over verbatim from `mark_failed.py`, but since the code is being moved into a new module it should be corrected now (change `"config": monitor_environment.monitor.config` to `"config": config`).

findings.title: Renamed/moved functions may break external imports and test patch targets
findings.body: `mark_failed_threshold` was renamed to `try_incident_threshold` and `create_issue_platform_occurrence` to `create_incident_occurrence`, and `SimpleCheckIn`, `get_failure_reason`, and `get_monitor_environment_context` were moved out of `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed` entirely, with no aliases left behind. Any code or tests outside this PR that import these names from `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed`, or that patch paths such as `sentry.monitors.logic.mark_failed.create_issue_platform_occurrence` / `mark_failed_threshold`, will fail with ImportError/AttributeError. Confirm that no remaining references exist (e.g., in test modules or other tasks) and that the corresponding test files are updated to the new module paths in this or a companion change.
